- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `659686d5cae79f8ae768a95135b528a3942c05a7` — the merge of head `b9f2cfec12f2bb83a85549c313557c95bade8887` into base `f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 659686d5cae79f8ae768a95135b528a3942c05a7 && git checkout 659686d5cae79f8ae768a95135b528a3942c05a7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55 b9f2cfec12f2bb83a85549c313557c95bade8887 && git checkout -B drift-repro f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55 && git merge --no-ff b9f2cfec12f2bb83a85549c313557c95bade8887

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f2b6cf230b4cddd795b854b044bbcd95e37b6f55` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `b9f2cfec12`
Local-runs: none

Scope: the net diff against the merge base (3 files, +258/−1):
- `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, `reconcileFederatedBindings`' report only;
- the new `federated-binding-policy-denied-report.test.ts`;
- the changeset.

Read with them:
- the card #25079, the claim 6314457843 and its re-declaration 6315166970 (option C, the seat's call on the dev's `needs_decision` 6314587078);
- the dev's `os-dev-report` 6317697898, read as claims;
- the PR body;
- `service-datasource`'s `availabilityOf` (`datasource-connection-service.ts:206`) and the engine's read refusal (`engine.ts:12030`). The seat read both at the re-declaration.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The split follows the recorded verdict, as re-declared: right.**
  - The pass reads `this.ql.listUnavailableDatasources()` once and keeps the names whose `kind` is `blocked`, the availability `service-datasource` gives `skipped-policy`.
  - An object with no driver whose effective datasource is in that set goes to `denied`. Every other object with no driver still goes to `unbound`. `unsupported` and `failed` are untouched.
  - No composition signal is read, so the result is the same on a serving boot, a `createHonoApp({ kernel })` embed and a migrate run. That was the point of C.
- **The info line is true and names what it should.**
  - The line reads `N federated (external) object(s) left unbound because the connect policy denied their datasource: <obj> -> datasource '<ds>', …`.
  - It goes on: `Every read against them is refused (DatasourceUnavailableError) until the policy allows that datasource`, and points back to the `connect denied by policy` line.
  - That matches the engine: `getDriver` throws `DatasourceUnavailableError(…, kind)` for an unavailable datasource. It is `info`, not silence, so #7737's "must stop being silent" holds. By the AGENTS.md degradation-log-level rule, a deliberate denial whose reads refuse loudly is functional, not a durability loss.
- **The ERROR is word for word what it was** for every class it still covers. Its counts are the `unbound`, `unsupported` and `failed` lengths, so they exclude the denied objects. A boot with only denied objects gets the info line and then the existing `debug` line, with no ERROR.
- **Nothing else moves.** The binding (`registerExternalObject`), the connect policy, the read results and the #9285 registry-read seam are unchanged.
- **The pins have teeth.**
  - Eleven cases:
    - the `blocked` case on a serving-shaped and a migrate-shaped context: one info line, no ERROR;
    - controls on both shapes (undeclared, `failed`, unsupported, registration threw): exactly one ERROR, counts unchanged;
    - a mixed boot: info for the denied object, an ERROR for the rest with the denied one excluded from its count.
  - In the ablation the routing line was restored to `unbound.push(`. Three went red (both `blocked` cases and the mixed one) and all eight controls stayed green. Restored blob-equal to `HEAD`.
- **The live reading matches.** `os migrate apply --yes` on the stock showcase, fresh file DB:
  - before: the denial line, then the ERROR;
  - after: the denial line, then the new info line naming `showcase_ext_customer` and `showcase_ext_order` on `showcase_external`, 0 ERROR lines, exit 0.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` for `@objectstack/objectql`: right for a boot log line's level and text, with no response, status, outcome, boot verdict or export moving.
- The changeset and the PR body carry the claim's `Clause-②: no (log text and level only: …)` line verbatim at a line start. They also carry `Metadata-protocol: none (…)`, which #25114 made required while this round ran; `none` is right, since nothing a metadata author writes changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Cross-lane:** none. `packages/runtime/src/federated-boot-binding.test.ts` (`domain:cli`) did not move and stays green: its datasource is undeclared, so it keeps the ERROR.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree` against today's `origin/main` (`f2b6cf230b`) is clean.
- **Deviations, all accepted:**
  - the `Metadata-protocol:` line (a new rule, value `none`);
  - no cross-lane file;
  - the runtime full suite measured before the last two `main` merges. Only #25086 moved a package in runtime's closure (objectql's `engine.ts`), and the objectql full suite was re-run after it; the diff touches no runtime file;
  - the session-URL PR footer and the dev's not subscribing (the seat holds the PR);
  - Check Changeset's PR-body half left to CI.
- **Open questions:** none.
- **Out of scope:** the `createHonoApp({ kernel })` / `http.server` observation is the reason option A was refused. Nothing reads it today, so nothing is filed.
- **The re-declaration's objection window:** no objection from `domain:devx` (the filer) or the maintainer on #25079 at this read.
- **CI on `b9f2cfec12`:** 5 of 40 check-runs still running at this read. The ACCEPT waits for green.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-25079-federated-report-migrate-run`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy`

**VERDICT: PASS**
